home_title: You don't have to say it out loud.
home_subtitle: A private health helper for women and girls. Speak or type — no name, no account, just help in your language.
home_pill_3: Never a diagnosis — always a real person
triage_intro: Answer a few questions. Nothing you share is tied to your name.
triage_duration: How many days has this been going on?
triage_severity: How severe does it feel? (1 = mild, 5 = very severe)
triage_freetext: Anything else you want to say, in your own words?
triage_pregnant: Are you pregnant, or could you be?
general_intro: For anyone, any symptom. Same triage engine as Sakhi, without the reproductive-health focus — answer a few questions to get routed to the right level of care.
result_not_diagnosis: This is not a diagnosis. Sakhi decides urgency and connects you to care.
cycle_subtitle: Track week by week. Sakhi checks for danger signs automatically.
dashboard_subtitle: Ranked by urgency, with the full reasoning behind every decision.
footer_disclaimer: Sakhi triages and routes. It never diagnoses, never prescribes, and always points toward a real clinician.
kbd_translit_hint: Type in English letters — “bukhaar” becomes your own script as you type.
anaemia_subtitle: Point your camera at your lower eyelid for a private pallor screen.
anaemia_guide: Gently pull down your lower eyelid and frame the pink inner surface in the circle.
anaemia_severity_mild: Mild flag — consider getting a blood test
anaemia_severity_moderate: Moderate flag — we recommend a blood test
anaemia_severity_strong: Strong flag — please get a blood test soon
anaemia_confidence_low: Capture quality: marginal — try again in better light
anaemia_disclaimer: This is a screening flag, not a haemoglobin measurement. Only a blood test can confirm or rule out anaemia.
anaemia_offline: Couldn't complete the screen — please try again or visit a health worker for a blood test.
anaemia_marginal: This capture may not be reliable — try again in better light for a more accurate screen.
anaemia_no_camera: Couldn't open the camera. Check permissions and try again.
anaemia_no_frame: Couldn't read the camera frame. Try again.
anaemia_reject_dark: Too dark — move to better light and try again.
anaemia_reject_bright: Too bright — move out of direct light and try again.
anaemia_reject_uniform: That doesn't look like an eyelid — frame the pink inner surface and try again.
anaemia_reject_nodata: Not enough of the eyelid was in the circle — move closer and try again.
anaemia_reject_notissue: Couldn't find the inner eyelid surface — pull the eyelid down a little more and try again.
anaemia_reject_generic: That capture couldn't be read — please try again.
account_optional_title: You do not need an account
account_optional_body: Everything here works without signing in — checking symptoms, the anaemia screen, helplines and your report. An account only remembers your language.
account_username_hint: Choose any name. Do not use your real name.
account_created: Account created. You can sign in now.
account_mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
account_rate_limited: Too many attempts. Please wait a few minutes.
account_stores: This account stores only your username and language. Your health results stay on this phone and are never sent with your account.
account_staff_note: Are you an ASHA or health worker?
offline_body: You can still check symptoms and read your saved report. Results will be sent when the network returns.
home_emergency_text: Skip the check-in. Call now — these numbers are free.
home_emergency_more: Women, children and mental health lines
home_services_title: What would you like to do?
home_services_sub: Tap any box. Nothing asks for your name.
home_desc_triage: Answer a few questions and find out how urgent it is. Takes two minutes.
home_desc_nearby: Call an ambulance and get a location code you can read out on the phone.
home_desc_helplines: Every national helpline — ambulance, women, children, mental health — in one list.
home_desc_anaemia: Point the camera at your lower eyelid for a straight yes or no on a blood test.
home_desc_prescription: Photograph a paper prescription and have it read back to you. Always confirm with your chemist.
home_desc_sakhi: Read trusted health information by topic.
home_desc_general: The same urgency check, for anyone — any age, any symptom.
home_desc_cycle: Log your period and see if your cycle is regular.
home_desc_pregnancy: Your week, trimester and due date from your last period. Danger signs checked.
home_desc_report: Turn everything you have done here into one printable record for a doctor.
home_desc_impact: How many people this has helped, and what it found.
home_promise_do_text: Tells you how urgent something is and where to go. If it is serious, an ASHA worker is alerted so a real person follows up.
home_promise_never_text: It never tells you what illness you have and never prescribes medicine. Only a doctor can do that.
home_promise_keep_text: No name, no phone number, no account. A health worker sees only how urgent your case is, never who you are.
nearby_intro: Call an ambulance and get a location code you can read out over the phone. This works even if the rest of Sakhi is down — it only needs your device's location and an internet connection.
nearby_signal_title: If you cannot get a signal
nearby_signal_tip1: Tell the dispatcher your village and panchayat name first.
nearby_signal_tip2: Then the nearest landmark — a temple, school, bus stop or PHC.
nearby_signal_tip3: Say which side of the road, and roughly how far from the landmark.
nearby_signal_tip4: Stay on the line. Do not hang up to call someone else.
nearby_digipin_text: A ten-character code from India Post that names a square about four metres across. It works anywhere in India, including places with no street address, and it is far easier to say correctly over a bad line than latitude and longitude.
locator_lead: Find your DIGIPIN first, then call. It is ten characters that name a spot about four metres across — far easier to say down a phone than directions, and it works where there is no street address.
locator_error_tip: If location will not work, tell the dispatcher the nearest landmark, village name and panchayat instead.
locator_read_aloud_label: Read this out to the dispatcher
locator_say_help: Say it one character at a time. It locates you to about four metres.
locator_privacy: Your location was worked out on this phone and was not sent to Sakhi's servers. It is shared only when you press call, copy or SMS.
impact_stat1_label: of India's doctors are concentrated in urban areas
impact_stat2_label: health workers per 10,000 people in India, vs. WHO's benchmark of 44.5
impact_stat3_label: higher doctor density in urban vs. rural India
impact_breakdown_restricted: The breakdown by urgency is visible to signed-in ASHA workers only.
impact_privacy_text: The doctor-shortage numbers above explain why care is hard to reach. They don't explain why a teenage girl with a period problem or a pregnancy scare often won't say it out loud — not to a male clinician, not in front of family. That's a shame-and-privacy problem, and it needs a private, no-name, voice-first entry point as much as it needs more clinics.
home_step1_text: Type or speak in your own language. No name, no phone number, no account.
home_step2_text: Self-care, see a doctor soon, or emergency — plus the reason why.
home_step3_text: See the nearest hospital, or an ASHA worker is alerted to follow up.
terms_page_intro: Please read this before using Sakhi.
terms_gate_hint: Scroll to the bottom to continue.
terms_s1_body: Sakhi is an independent, non-commercial student project, built for the SkillUp Hackathon with IBM SkillsBuild. It is not an official Government of India service, is not affiliated with any ministry, and issues no official document.
terms_s2_body: Sakhi triages how urgent your situation is and routes you to the right level of care. If it is serious, an ASHA worker is alerted so a real person follows up.
terms_s3_body: Sakhi never diagnoses an illness and never prescribes medicine. It always points you toward a real clinician. Nothing here replaces a doctor's judgement.
terms_s4_title: If you disclose abuse or self-harm
terms_s4_body: Anything you share that suggests abuse or self-harm is routed straight to a real person. It is never handled by the AI model alone.
terms_s5_body: No name, phone number or account is required. Nothing here is tied to your identity. A health worker sees only how urgent your case is, never who you are. You can delete any session's data at any time.
terms_s6_title: Government schemes mentioned in your report
terms_s6_body: Scheme names and ministries are cited so entitlements can be verified at source. Scheme terms are set by the issuing ministry and may change.
terms_s7_body: Call 108 (ambulance) or 112 directly. Do not wait for Sakhi to respond — these numbers are free and immediate.
terms_s8_body: You confirm you have read and understood this page. You can read it again at any time from the link at the bottom of every page.
